claims.text: A new DFT-based computational method can accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The method is applicable to high-entropy alloys in their initial, unprocessed state.
The proposed intervention uses DFT to predict phonon thermal conductivity.
The approach is intended for thermal-insulation applications in high-temperature environments.
Phonon dispersion and lattice dynamics are the structural mediators relevant to the prediction.
Ab initio calculations and molecular-dynamics simulations can be combined to model high-entropy alloys.
Ab initio calculations and molecular-dynamics simulations can predict phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys.
The new method will improve predictions relative to current traditional methods.
Improved identification of low-phonon-conductivity alloys will lead to enhanced thermal-insulation performance.
Current traditional methods provide the baseline predictions against which the new method should be compared.
Computational cost limits the applicability of the proposed method.
Limited accuracy constrains the applicability of the proposed method.
Experimental thermal-conductivity measurements can benchmark the predicted phonon thermal conductivity values.
Raman spectroscopy or inelastic neutron scattering can be used in the proposed benchmark of phonon thermal conductivity.
A significant deviation between predicted and measured values would falsify the hypothesis.
